A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Large Continual Instruction Assistant and contain the complete 25-page paper, including Appendices A–Q. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the prose, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v4 reports original continual instruction tuning experiments on LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and T5/InstrDialog, together with ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the proposed method’s multimodal results in Tables 1–7 and dialogue results in Table 8.

M1.justification: The adaptive EMA procedure, approximations, instruction grouping, and inference selection remain unchanged. Appendix E still specifies Eq. (45) for implementation, and Algorithm 1 is unchanged; the Appendix P revision concerns the supporting derivation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight multimodal datasets, the 19-task InstrDialog stream, and the same dialogue examples and instruction variants. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within Tables 1–3 and Table 8. For example, Table 3 retains LoRA Fine-Tune and PGP, while Table 8 retains the same fine-tuning, AdapterCL, regularization, AGEM, replay, and multitask comparisons.

E3.justification: The model configurations, frozen/trainable components, training settings, task orders, instruction variants, and evaluation metrics are unchanged in Section 5.1 and Appendices J–O. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablation in Table 6, EMA-weight sensitivity in Table 7, task-order and instruction robustness analyses in Tables 4–5 and Figures 4–5, and qualitative cases in Figures 6–10.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, while the multimodal tables retain point estimates. No run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted outcomes, rankings, and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 retains 64.64 Avg.ACC, 1.93 Forgetting, and 66.33 New.ACC for Ours, and Table 8 retains its 39.8 average ROUGE-L.

T1.justification: Appendix P revises Eq. (60), removing the displacement factor d = Θ_t − Θ*_{t−1} from the numerator and the final factor of the quadratic-form denominator. The revised expression uses [d^T H]^{-1} instead of a scalar reciprocal involving d^T H d, without additional assumptions. The remaining derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: adaptive EMA for stability/plasticity balance, limited parameter expansion through instruction grouping, model-independent applicability, and strong continual tuning performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of robustness, forgetting, hallucination examples, and instruction-group efficiency remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the same computational-resource limitation and current focus on image and text tasks.

D1.justification: Appendices E, H, J, and Q retain the same implementation formula, TF-IDF/sklearn description, hyperparameters, and pseudocode. The code-access link is unchanged, with no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Section 2 and Appendix G retain the same discussion of earlier methods, including the comparison with L2P and EProj.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the equation references preceding Eq. (10): Eq. (56) becomes Eq. (4), and Eq. (57) becomes Eq. (8). The arXiv version stamp is updated; the prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 removes the repeated paper-title headers and slightly changes the display spacing around Eq. (60). Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–10 retain their visual content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: Under Appendix P’s vector/Hessian notation, v4’s Eq. (60) gives a scalar ratio consistent with Eq. (59), whereas v5 replaces it with an unspecified inverse of the row vector d^T H. This introduces a localized mathematical defect in the high-dimensional justification. The corrected references in Section 4.2 improve navigation, but do not offset that defect; the implemented method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
